entities.summary: James I was King of Scots from 1406 to 1437. The youngest of three sons, he was born in Dunfermline Abbey to King Robert III and his wife Annabella Drummond. His older brother David, Duke of Rothesay died under suspicious circumstances while being detained by their uncle, Robert, Duke of Albany. His other brother, Robert, died young. Fears for James's safety grew through the winter of 1405/6 and plans were made to send him to France. In February 1406, James was forced to take refuge in the castle of the Bass Rock in the Firth of Forth after his escort was attacked by supporters of Archibald, 4th Earl of Douglas.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: James I's reign marked a significant turning point in Scottish history, as he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between Scotland, England, and France. His diplomatic efforts helped establish a fragile peace with England, which lasted for over a century.
